Write a table note

Source: R/notes.R
apa_note.Rd

Makes the text of an APA-style table note from what a table function recorded about how the table was made. The text is a starting point: edit it or add to it as needed.

Usage

apa_note(x, collapse = " ")

Arguments

x

a table made by apa_anova(), apa_htest(), apa_parameters(), apa_loadings(), or apa_factor_cor()

collapse

string that joins the sentences. Use NULL to get a character vector with one sentence per element.

Value

character

Details

For apa_anova() tables, the note can say

  • which type of sums of squares was used,

  • which effects have sphericity-corrected degrees of freedom (for afex models, only effects involving a within-subjects factor with more than two levels are corrected),

  • what the effect size (and MSE, for afex models) stands for, and

  • what stars or bold values mean.

For apa_loadings() tables, the note can say

  • how the factors were extracted and rotated (e.g., "Principal axis factoring with oblimin rotation"), and that loadings after an oblique rotation are pattern coefficients,

  • which loadings are omitted (min_loading) or bolded (bold_max),

  • what the h^2^, u^2^, and Complexity columns stand for, and

  • that the cumulative proportion of variance is approximate when the factors are correlated.

For apa_factor_cor() tables, the note says how the factors were extracted and rotated.

For apa_htest() tables, the note can say

  • which tests were done (e.g., Welch's t tests) and what the groups were compared with or the variables were correlated with,

  • that p-values are one-sided, if they are,

  • how Cohen's d (or Hedges' g) was standardized,

  • what the effect size and its confidence interval stand for, and

  • what stars or bold values mean.

For apa_parameters() tables of regression models (lm, glm, polr, clm, lme4, and glmmTMB models, or a list of models), the note can say

  • which robust standard errors were used (e.g., vcov = "HC3"),

  • how the degrees of freedom of mixed-model t tests were approximated (Kenward-Roger or Satterthwaite),

  • that ordinal-model thresholds are not tested,

  • the scale of the zero-inflation and dispersion coefficients of glmmTMB models,

  • what the standardized coefficient (\(\beta\)), exponentiated coefficient (e.g., OR), confidence interval, and model-comparison (e.g., \(\Delta R^2\)) columns stand for, and

  • what stars or bold values mean.

Abbreviations are defined from the abbreviation slot of each column's column_format(), so a note defines every abbreviated header that has a definition. To define another header, or to change a definition, set the slot in the column_formats passed to the table function (or set the default with apa7_defaults()):

cf <- column_formats()
cf$Sum_Squares@abbreviation <- "sum of squares"
apa_anova(fit, anova_parameters = c("Parameter", "Sum_Squares", "df", "F", "p"),
          column_formats = cf)

The sentences are in APA order: general notes first, then probability notes. The text does not start with "Note." because apaquarto adds it. With apaquarto, make the table in one chunk and display it in another, using the note as the apa-note chunk option. Write apa7::apa_note() there, because in documents with cached chunks, chunk options can be evaluated before library(apa7) takes effect:

```{r}
#| label: anova-fit
tbl <- apa_anova(fit, type = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-anova
#| tbl-cap: Analysis of Variance
#| apa-note: !expr apa7::apa_note(tbl)
tbl
```

The information is stored in an "apa_note" attribute of the table. dplyr functions such as mutate() and filter() keep it, but some operations (e.g., bind_rows() and joins) drop it, so call apa_note() on the table that the table function returned.

Examples

d <- mtcars
d$cyl <- factor(d$cyl)
d$am <- factor(d$am)
fit <- aov(mpg ~ cyl * am, data = d)
tbl <- apa_anova(fit, starred = "F")
apa_note(tbl)
#> [1] "Sums of squares are sequential (Type I). *&eta;*^2^~p~ = partial eta squared. ^\\* ^*p* < .05. ^\\*\\* ^*p* < .01. ^\\*\\*\\* ^*p* < .001."

if (requireNamespace("afex", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(obk.long, package = "afex")
  fit_afex <- afex::aov_ez(
    "id", "value", obk.long,
    between = "treatment", within = "phase", fun_aggregate = mean
  )
  apa_note(apa_anova(fit_afex))
}
#> Contrasts set to contr.sum for the following variables: treatment
#> [1] "Type III sums of squares. Degrees of freedom and *p*-values for effects involving Phase are Greenhouse–Geisser corrected. *MSE* = mean square error; *&eta;*^2^~G~ = generalized eta squared."

# Factor analysis
fit_fa <- psych::fa(Harman74.cor$cov, 4, fm = "pa", rotate = "varimax")
apa_loadings(fit_fa, min_loading = .3, communality = TRUE) |>
  apa_note()
#> [1] "Principal axis factoring with varimax rotation. Loadings smaller than .30 in absolute value are omitted. *h*^2^ = communality."

# Regression
lm(mpg ~ cyl + wt, data = mtcars) |>
  apa_parameters(starred = "p") |>
  apa_note()
#> [1] "&beta; = standardized coefficient. ^\\* ^*p* < .05. ^\\*\\* ^*p* < .01. ^\\*\\*\\* ^*p* < .001."
